_comment: Single source of truth for path -> docs/rules/<domain> routing.
scripts/inject/route_domains.py. Adding/renaming a domain = edit THIS file only.
ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING. Rules are evaluated top-to-bottom per path:
- mode 'additive': if any glob matches, its domains are added (deduped).
- mode 'fallback': applied ONLY if no domain has been collected YET at this
position. A fallback must stay BELOW the additive rules it defers to, and
additive rules placed AFTER a fallback still stack on top of it. This is why
Reordering changes behavior — see test-inject-patterns.sh firebase regression.
Globs use fnmatch semantics (matched case-sensitively, '*' spans '/'), matching

bash [[ == ]] in the original hooks. Todo 244 (2026-07-02) resolved the deferred 'agents'/'exclusions' question: agent routing stays in the two orchestrator files (.claude/agents/*-orchestrator.md), NOT here — the fleet shrank to 8 reviewers (4 generics consolidated into cross-cutting-reviewer) and the orchestrators' tables carry primary/secondary semantics this flat path->domain format can't express.
Consequence of the testing-rule-before-ts-fallback order: a web non-.tsx test
file (e.g. web/src/App.spec.ts) resolves to 'testing' only — the *.ts fallback
is suppressed by the earlier testing match. This matches the old inject hook;
the old kimi/codify tables gave typescript+testing. Blessed (fail-safe: drops a
checklist hint, never blocks). .tsx web specs keep typescript via web/src/*.tsx.

rules._why: Editing a dependency manifest or a workflow used to inject only _discipline.md — never security.md — so the 'try a bump before suppressing a vuln' rule was invisible at exactly the moment it mattered. Order is load-bearing: this sits after the backend/*.py fallback and before firebase, and no .github/ or manifest path matches any other rule, so there is no fallback interaction.

Every top-level scripts/*.py IS a security scanner — new_vuln_gate.py (the new-advisory gate), check_suppressions.py (the suppression validator), check_flutter_security.py, sync_alarm_todo.py — and all four routed to NO domain, so editing the security tooling injected no security rules. Same failure as the .github/* rule above, one directory over: the rule that names a file was invisible to whoever edits that file. Additive and placed here so the testing rule below still stacks (test_*.py in this directory resolves to security,testing). Added by codify from fix/todo-356-root-npm-manifest-audit.
